general_information.Description: The course focuses on the general knowledge of the culture of Tourism and Hospitality, identifying core issues of the culture that relate to different behaviours, habits, tradition and civilization. On the other hands, the course also helps students understand the intersections between touristic, hotel and culinary cultures and with other sciences. Besides, the course brings up the deep analysis of tourism and hospitality culture in relationship with world culture, cultural studies, ideology, sociology, art, etc. The Culture of Tourism and Hospitality is not only the study of all cultures in the world, but its primary purpose is also to see the cultural circumstances, the conditions of formation of cultures. Therefore, it helps students understand the cultural perspective and details of the development, which capture the essence, the features, rules of development and interaction between them.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: - Internet - Net-Challenge Simulation Software (CD accompany with the textbook)
general_information.Note: Progress marks: - Participation: 10% - 03 Progress test: 90% Conditions to pass: Each progress mark: > 0 Grade Average >= 5/10

assessments.Question Type: Each student shoud make at least 1 individual presentation, case analysis during the course in front of the class. Topics will be varied based on the topics in the textbook.
assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.Question Type: Four or five students per group. Groups and groups ideas are determined on the third session of the course. Work will be break down into stages and examined during the course. Final work to be submitted prior to the presentation of the topic.
assessments.No Question: Minimum length of the group assignment should be 10 pages, excluding appendices
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on topics of studied units
assessments.Note: All assignments should be typed with 13-point font, and must be submitted in soft copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission Evaluation will be based on both presentation and written report (recommended 30%, 70% accordingly)

assessments.Question Type: Four or five students per group. Competency is to be demonstrated by effectively preparing and serving beverage in accordance with the performance criteria and the range listed within the practical learning sessions.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the practical learning sessions of the course.
assessments.Note: Competency in this unit may be assessed through: Demonstration of skills on mixing different (in quantity) international alcoholic beverages in a prescribed timeframe; utilizing systematic liquor pouring and proper bar measurement; mixing of alcoholic concoction showmanship skill techniques. The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

assessments.Question Type: Each student must be assessed through practical demonstration in a simulated workplace environment where beverage ingredients and equipment are provided. Competency is to be demonstrated by effectively preparing and serving beverage in accordance with the performance criteria and the range listed within the practical learning sessions.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the practical learning sessions of the course.
assessments.Note: Competency in this unit may be assessed through: - Observation shall be done on the proper classification of alcoholic beverages and glasses; proper mixing procedures on several cocktails and the uses and maintenance of different bar tools and equipment. - Direct observation of student providing advice to customers or colleagues on wine and its proper serving procedures.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice, exercises or essay questions
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Quizzes will test for knowledge of subjects in the chapter assigned for that day.
assessments.Note: These quizzes will be given at various times during class (beginning, middle or end). Total number of quizzes: 2

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice . Other types of questions may be included.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: The questions/ exercises will cover the lectures, class discussions, activities, exercises, and textbook.
assessments.Note: Not allow to use any document/information in any form in exam room

schedule.Student Materials: Group assignment implementation Including: Presentation + Report + a practical video (optional) Presentation: For the 30-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates and lecturer with slides, a practical video and reports about your group project. Report: To accomplish this group, you need to: • Conduct a particular alcoholic beverage (spirits, wine, beer…) • Prepare and discuss information of the chosen alcoholic beverage: the brief history of the beverage, the development of the bar and beverage industry in Vietnam, different types of the beverage and appropriate matches with food, storage and equipment requirements of common types of the beverage, how to serve the beverage… • Have a group proposal (This is the mission done at group assignment) • Writing a final report • Reporting the whole group project at the end of semester Include the following sections in your report: PARTS OF FORMAL REPORTS 1. Preliminary Section Title Page Table of Contents 2. Body Introduction Analysis Conclusions & Recommendations 3. Supplementary Section Appendix (If any) Reference List Based on chapter 3,5,6,7,8 of The Bar & Beverage Book textbook
